planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun to partial shade; Ballerina is a compact, classic cranesbill selection well suited to rock gardens and border edges.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun to partial shade. Ballerina bears pale pink to lilac-pink flowers delicately veined in deep purple-red, opening on a low, compact, mounding plant that fits well in rock gardens, border edges, and small-space plantings where larger hardy geranium cultivars would be out of scale. It blooms heavily in late spring and early summer, with some sporadic rebloom if sheared back after the main flush. Its finely cut, aromatic foliage adds texture even when not in bloom, and the plant is generally trouble-free, tolerating heat and drought reasonably well once established. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, average soil in full sun to partial shade; Orion bears unusually large flowers for a hardy geranium on a vigorous, mounding plant.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, average soil in full sun to partial shade. Orion bears exceptionally large, vivid blue-violet flowers with a small white eye, among the biggest individual blooms of any hardy geranium cultivar, opening in a heavy flush in late spring and early summer on a vigorous, mounding plant. Cutting the plant back hard after the first flush often produces a worthwhile rebloom later in the season. Its bold flower size and rich color make it a standout in a mixed perennial border, and it tolerates a range of soil conditions with reasonable drought tolerance once established. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor and flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, average soil in full sun to partial shade; Brookside is a vigorous, finely textured cranesbill valued for clear sky-blue flowers over a long bloom season.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, average soil in full sun to partial shade. Brookside bears clear sky-blue flowers with a small white center over finely cut, ferny foliage, opening in a heavy flush in late spring and continuing sporadically through summer, especially if cut back after the main bloom. Its vigorous, spreading habit and fine foliage texture make it a useful filler weaving through and under other perennials in a mixed border without becoming aggressive. It tolerates heat reasonably well for a hardy geranium and needs only occasional division every few years in spring to maintain vigor and control spread.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun to partial shade; Espresso is grown as much for its dark chocolate-brown foliage as for its pink flowers.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun to partial shade; more sun deepens the dark foliage color, though some afternoon shade helps in the hottest climates. Espresso bears deeply lobed leaves in a rich chocolate-brown to bronze-purple that holds its color through the growing season, providing striking foliage contrast well beyond its modest clusters of small pink flowers in late spring and early summer. Its low, spreading habit works well as a foreground accent or foliage contrast plant paired with silver or chartreuse companions in a mixed border. It is generally trouble-free and tolerates average garden conditions with reasonable drought tolerance once established; divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.
